correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=3 and every complex z, normalization D=n-1+|z|²>0. Weyl conjugation diagonalizes the rank-one projector Gram operator: eigenvalue n|B(a,b)|²/D², so rank counts exactly nonzero ambiguities. From v=(z,1,...,1): B(0,0)=D; B(0,b≠0)=|z|²-1; B(a≠0,0)=n-2+2Re(z); B(a≠0,b≠0)=(z-1)+(conj(z)-1)ω^(ab). For δ=z-1≠0, mixed zeros correspond to ω^(ab)= -δ/conj(δ); if not an n-th root none occur. For root ω^r and a with gcd(a,n)=d dividing r, there are d residue solutions b; φ(n/d) such nonzero a, and when r=0 exactly one b=0 for each nonzero a is discarded, yielding C_n(r). The axes and mixed index classes are disjoint; all intersections of parameter loci are therefore additive. At z=1 the n distinct modulated rays form a Fourier ONB and rank n. At z=1+it (t real nonzero), c=1 and C_n(0)=Σ_{a=1}^{n-1}(gcd(a,n)-1), vanishing iff n prime. At z=2+2i, c=(3-4i)/5 has trace 6/5; roots of unity have algebraic-integer traces, and rational algebraic integers are integral, so no n admits mixed zeros; axes are also nonzero. An independent NumPy direct projector-matrix checker matched 35 (n,z) ranks for n=3..9, and an independent exact integer count matched every ab=r fiber for n=3..14. Finite checks are corroborative, not proof of the all-n claim.

value.rationale: The one-coordinate perturbation of the constant cyclic window is a geometrically and experimentally natural minimal symmetry breaking. The exact rank of its n² Gabor POVM projectors, including every composite-modulus zero-divisor defect and the complex exceptional parameter geometry, is an independently useful natural tomography invariant beyond generic injectivity. The same-family prime case and general spectral tool are credited to prior work, not counted anew.
